title: Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions
description: The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) asserts that all non-trivial zeros of Dirichlet L-functions L(s, χ) lie on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2. We formalize GRH, prove equivalences between formulations, and axiomatize its dramatic consequences: improved PNT for arithmetic progressions (error O(√x log x)), effective Linnik bound (least prime O(q² log² q)), elimination of Siegel zeros, and effective class number bounds.

overview.historicalContext:
The Riemann Hypothesis (1859) for the zeta function was generalized by Piltz (1884) to Dirichlet L-functions. GRH predicts that ALL non-trivial zeros of L(s, χ) for ANY Dirichlet character χ lie on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2.

GRH is strictly stronger than RH: it addresses infinitely many L-functions, not just ζ(s). A proof of GRH would have immediate, dramatic consequences for prime distribution in arithmetic progressions, computational number theory, and cryptography.

The consequences are well-studied: under GRH, the error term in the PNT for APs improves from O(x · exp(-c√log x)) to O(√x · log x), Linnik's bound drops from the best unconditional exponent L ≤ 5 (Xylouris, 2011) to effectively L = 2, i.e., O(q² log² q). The Montgomery-Vaughan improvement (1977) of character sums from O(√q log q) to O(√q log log q) under GRH remains one of the deepest consequences.

GRH also eliminates Siegel zeros entirely. Siegel's 1935 ineffective bound |L(1,χ)| ≫ q^{-ε} (with an uncomputable constant) is replaced under GRH by the effective bound |L(1,χ)| ≥ C/(log q)². Goldfeld (1985) resolved the class number problem using Gross-Zagier, but the unconditional bound h(d) ≫ (log|d|)^{1-ε} remains far weaker than the GRH prediction h(d) ≥ C√|d|/log|d|.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question**: Does the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis hold for all Dirichlet L-functions? That is, for every Dirichlet character χ modulo q, do all zeros of L(s, χ) with 0 < Re(s) < 1 satisfy Re(s) = 1/2?

**Status**: OPEN. No proof or counterexample exists. Computational verification extends to billions of zeros.

**Key formalization**: We prove GRH ↔ GRH_right_half (no zeros with Re(s) > 1/2), using the functional equation symmetry. We axiomatize all major consequences and prove theorems connecting them.
overview.text: The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) asserts that all non-trivial zeros of Dirichlet L-functions L(s, χ) lie on the critical line Re(s) = 1/2. We formalize GRH, prove equivalences between formulations, and axiomatize its dramatic consequences for prime distribution, character sums, and class numbers.
overview.proofStrategy:
We formalize GRH in three layers:

**1. Definitions**: GRH_for_character (per-character), GRH (all characters), GRH_right_half (no zeros with Re > 1/2).

**2. Proved equivalences**: GRH ↔ GRH_right_half via the functional equation axiom. GRH_right_half = GRH_via_log_derivative.

**3. Consequences (axiomatized)**: Improved PNT for APs, effective Linnik bound, Montgomery-Vaughan character sum improvement, effective L(1,χ) lower bound, class number bounds. Each is stated precisely with the GRH hypothesis.

**4. Connections**: GRH eliminates Siegel zeros (proved from definitions), comprehensive nonvanishing for σ > 1/2 (proved combining GRH, Dirichlet, Euler product).
keyInsights: GRH ↔ GRH_right_half: The functional equation sends a zero at s to one at 1-s, so 'no zeros with Re(s) > 1/2' is equivalent to 'all zeros on Re(s) = 1/2'
GRH immediately eliminates Siegel zeros: any Siegel zero β ∈ (1-c/log q, 1) satisfies β > 1/2, contradicting GRH
Under GRH, the PNT error for APs drops from O(x exp(-c√log x)) to O(√x log x) — a dramatic improvement
Under GRH, the least prime in an AP drops from O(q^5) to O(q² log² q) — effective Linnik
GRH gives EFFECTIVE lower bounds on L(1,χ), unlike Siegel's INEFFECTIVE bound
prerequisites: Complex analysis (zeros of analytic functions, functional equations)
Number theory (primes in arithmetic progressions, class numbers)

conclusion.summary: This formalization captures the GRH for Dirichlet L-functions: its precise statement, equivalences between formulations, and the dramatic consequences that would follow from a proof. The key proved result is GRH ↔ GRH_right_half via the functional equation. All major consequences (PNT improvement, Linnik improvement, Siegel zero elimination, class number bounds) are axiomatized with precise quantitative statements.
conclusion.implications:
**If GRH is proved**: All consequences become theorems — improved PNT for APs, effective Linnik bound, no Siegel zeros, effective class number bounds, improved character sums, deterministic primality testing.

**For Mathlib**: Would require the full machinery of Dirichlet L-function theory including analytic continuation, functional equation, and explicit formula.

**Connection to OQ01**: GRH eliminates Siegel zeros, resolving the central question of OQ01.
openQuestions: Is GRH true for all Dirichlet L-functions? (THE open question — Millennium Prize level)
Can GRH be proved for specific families of characters? (e.g., quadratic characters)
What is the best unconditional approximation to GRH? (zero-free regions)
Can computational methods provide stronger evidence? (extending zero verification)

GRH eliminates Siegel zeros (the central question of OQ01), providing the effective lower bound L(1,χ) ≫ 1/(log q)²
GRH generalizes RH from the single Riemann zeta function to ALL Dirichlet L-functions
GRH refines the PNT error term for primes in APs from O(x exp(-c√log x)) to O(√x log x), and removes restrictions on the modulus q
The divergence of the prime reciprocal series is a consequence of the PNT; GRH strengthens the rate of divergence for primes in arithmetic progressions
